summary: Handrio Nurhan is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a BA in Liberal Arts at Soka University of America (2011–2015), an MA at Texas Tech University (2016–2018), and a PhD at Boston University in 2018.
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He was a faculty member at Haverford College, where his posts are attested in 2009 and 2019.

Hanna Havnevik is a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of Oslo as Professor (attested 2006–2008) and later Professor Emerita (attested 2026).
Hanna Wałkówska (1921–2013) was an Indologist. She studied at the University of Breslau from circa 1946 to 1951 under Ludwik Skurzak and subsequently held a post there from circa 1951 to 1991.

Hannah Gould works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She studied at the University of Melbourne and University of Oxford, and held posts at Monash University, St Vincent's Hospital Melbourne, and the University of Melbourne (Lecturer, 2024).

Hannes Sköld (1886–1930) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Gothenburg and Lund University, where he later served as Docent of Slavonic Languages (1920) and Docent of Comparative IE Linguistics (1926).

Hanns Oertel (1868–1952) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After earning his Ph.D. under William Dwight Whitney at Yale, he taught at Yale, the University of Marburg, and held a chair at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt (1930–2017) was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ludwig Alsdorf and served as a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles from 1965 to 2000.

Hans Adolf Dietrich Hartmann (1909–2000) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Marburg, Berlin, and Dublin, later serving as Professor of Comparative IE Linguistics at the University of Hamburg from 1953 to 1978.

Hans Conon von der Gabelentz (1807–1874) was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the universities of Leipzig and Göttingen between 1825 and 1828 and founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft.

Hans Delbrück (1848–1929) was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held posts at Frederick William University Berlin (1885) and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1883–1921).

Hans E. Kauffmann (1899–1985) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert von Heine-Geldern and earned a PhD from the University of Zurich (~1930–1934).

Hans Frederik Hendriksen (1913–1989) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Copenhagen. He served as Professor at Uppsala University (1947–1951) and subsequently as Professor of Indian-Oriental Philology at the University of Copenhagen (1951–1983).

Hans Haas (1868–1934) worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Erlangen-Nuremberg, he held posts at German Theological High School, the University of Tokyo, the University of Jena, and the University of Leipzig (from 1915).

Hans Harder (born 1966) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the universities of Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg (doctoral supervisor Rahul Peter Das), later serving as an Assistent at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007).
Hans Hartog (born 1912) was an Indologist. He studied at Tübingen, Bethel, and Munich before earning his Ph.D. at the University of Marburg (1937–1939) under doctoral supervisor Friedrich Heiler.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder (1896–1957) was a scholar of Iranian studies and religion who studied at Breslau and Berlin. He was a professor at Königsberg, Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin (1931–1944), and the University of Göttingen (1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock (born 1938) is a linguist and Indologist. He completed graduate studies at Northwestern and Yale (under Warren Crawford Cowgill) and served as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~1980–2007).

Hans Jensen Jørgensen (1886–1954) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Marburg, Munich, and Kiel (PhD 1906–1911 under Emil Sieg), and worked as a scientific assistant at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1912 to 1919.

Hans Josef Nolte (1857–1916) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg in 1894 and served as Director of Gymnasium Papenburg from 1904 to 1916.
